newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-GOOCH CAN ONLY WATCH AND WAIT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-GOOCH CAN ONLY WATCH AND WAIT.

text.p: Graham Gooch ended as a frustrated spectator on the opening day of his farewell championship match for Essex as a Reuben Spiring century eased Worcestershire into a strong position on 328-6 on Wednesday.
Gooch, celebrating his 44th birthday, led out Essex at Chelmsford but could only watch on as the visitors refused to be overawed by the occasion.

Spiring scored one of seven centuries around the country as batsmen got the upper hand everywhere, except at Cheltenham where Durham were rolled over for just 86 by Gloucestershire, and at Lord's, where 19 wickets fell in the match between Middlesex and Kent.
Peter Such picked up three wickets for Essex but Spiring, scored an unbeaten 119 and with support from Vikram Solanki (60) in a sixth-wicket stand of 151 helped boost the total by the close of play.
Martin McCague claimed six for 49 as Kent hit back in style against Middlesex, who ended the day on 103 for nine, having earlier dismissed the visitors for 208.

Simon Brown claimed four wickets but half-centuries from opener Matt Windows (75), Shaun Young (52) and skipper Mark Alleyne (77 not out) earned Gloucestershire a lead of 167 going into the second day against dismal Durham.
Third-placed Gloucestershire recovered from 28 for three to reach 253 for five after John Morris (32) and Nick Speak (22) had been the only visiting batsmen to reach double figures.

The last eight Durham wickets fell for 25 runs as they collapsed to their lowest first-innings score since they came into the championship, Alleyne claiming five for 14 and Tasmanian all-rounder Young bagging three for nine.

At Southampton, Andrew Flintoff scored a maiden century (117) and Mike Watkinson (102 not out) also reached three figures during a fifth-wicket stand of 214 as Lancashire piled up 423 for five against Hampshire.
Left-hander Matthew Dowman made an unbeaten championship-best 125 as Nottinghamshire ended the day on 296 for nine against defending champions Leicestershire at Grace Road.
